Skilled in building rapid prototypes using Python (FastAPI, PySpark), React, TypeScript, and 2D/3D interactive simulations in Unity (C#). summary:
Field Shift is an interactive agroclimatic decision-support web application that helps smallholder farmers adapt planting schedules and multi-season crop rotations to shifting climate patterns. Built with React, TypeScript, Recharts, and Framer Motion, the platform integrates live NASA POWER Agroclimatology (AG) satellite telemetry—retrieving root-zone soil moisture (GWETROOT), rainfall (PRECTOTCORR), air temperature (T2M), and relative humidity (RH2M) across 25+ Sri Lankan and global agricultural zones or any custom GPS coordinate.

Field Shift directly addresses climate-driven crop failure by adjusting raw satellite moisture with local soil-retention physics, projecting 30-day seasonal trajectories from a 5-year NASA climatology baseline, and providing an interactive What-If Climate Stress Simulator. By ranking traditional monocropping against soil-restoring legumes and drought-hardy rotations, Field Shift transforms complex orbital observations into clear, actionable guidance—protecting smallholder harvests, seed investments, and long-term soil health.
details:
Field Shift helps smallholder farmers adapt planting schedules and crop rotations to shifting climate conditions. Users pick from 25+ global and Sri Lankan zones (or use custom GPS coordinates) to pull live NASA POWER Agroclimatology (AG) data—root-zone soil moisture (GWETROOT), rainfall (PRECTOTCORR), temperature (T2M), and relative humidity (RH2M)—alongside a 5-year seasonal baseline for a 30-day future outlook. Our agronomic engine adjusts raw satellite moisture for local soil types, lets users test drought/warming scenarios via a What-If Climate Stress Simulator, and ranks three crop-rotation strategies (monocrop vs. legume rotation vs. drought-resilient crops).

Benefits & Intended Impact Field Shift protects smallholder seed investments from drought or flood failure, promotes soil-restoring crop diversification, and translates complex orbital data into plain-language guidance usable by farmers and extension officers worldwide.

Tools, Languages & Software Used

  • Frontend & Visuals: React, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, Recharts, Framer Motion, Lucide Icons
  • Data & APIs: NASA POWER API (community=AG), W3C Browser Geolocation API
  • Build & Hosting: Vite, Git/GitHub, Vercel (developed in VS Code with GitHub Copilot)

How It Is Creative Instead of acting as a passive weather viewer, Field Shift is an interactive climate stress sandbox—letting farmers simulate +4°C warming or -50% rainfall and watch their 30-day soil moisture curve and #1 recommended crop rotation adapt in real time.

Key Factors Considered We accounted for NASA's 0.5° × 0.625° grid resolution by adding local soil-retention multipliers and an expandable "Satellite Gaps & Local Verification" checklist, filtered -999 missing-data values, and visually separated observed satellite history from 5-year seasonal projections.
